criteria.semantics: A native <input> of the field's input type, named by a visible <label for> (never a placeholder), its hint and its error in text the input points at with aria-describedby, required and invalid stated with aria-required and aria-invalid.

keyboard.outcome: Focus moves to the input and is strongly visually indicated.
Enters text in the input; a checkbox field toggles with Space instead.

criteria.name: The field's label, the same words as the visible label.
criteria.role: The input's type: text input, email, password, checkbox and so on.
criteria.group: The hint, then the error, read after the label; the form's label names the group the field is in.
criteria.state: Required when the field is required, invalid when it carries an error.

setting.statement: WHEN I set my text size to 200% I SEE the label, the input's text, the hint and the error grow with it, with no loss of information.
WHEN I zoom the page to 400% I SEE the label above or beside its input, the hint and error under it, and no horizontal scrolling.

check.statement: The face emits a native <input> element.
WHEN I use the Tab key I SEE focus reach the input: it is in the tab order, not disabled and with no negative tabindex.
WHEN the input has focus I SEE a focus ring of at least 2px in the focus color.
I SEE a label that stays visible, tied to the input by for and id, with the field's label as its text.
I SEE the hint and the error as text after the input, which the input names in aria-describedby, hint first.
A required field says so: aria-required is true exactly when the field is required.
A field with an error says so: aria-invalid is true exactly when the field carries an error, and the error is in words, not only in color.
WHEN I Tab to the input with a desktop screen reader (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver) I HEAR its purpose is clear and I HEAR it identify itself as its input type (text input, email, checkbox).
WHEN I Tab to the input I HEAR the hint and any error read after the label, and the form's name when it is in a named group.
WHEN the field is required or invalid I HEAR it expressed as required or invalid.
WHEN I swipe to the input with a mobile screen reader (TalkBack, VoiceOver) I HEAR the same name, role, hint and state, and the on-screen keyboard appears on a double tap.

criteria.semantics: A text input in the window's tab order with its label above it (an asterisk when required; a click on the label focuses the input), its hint under it in text and its error in the danger color and in words; a checkbox field is one focusable control drawn ☐ or ☑ beside its label. Input goes through the platform's text services (IME composition on all three). Once GPUI exposes a tree: an AccessKit TextInput (MultilineTextInput for a text area) or CheckBox node named by its label, described by the hint and then the error, required and invalid as the field is, with its value and text selection (AXTextField or AXTextArea and AXCheckBox on macOS, the Edit and CheckBox control types on Windows, an entry and a check box on AT-SPI).

keyboard.outcome: Focus moves to the input, in reading order, and the focus ring shows.
Focus moves back to the control before it, wrapping to the last.
Enters text in the input, through the IME when one composes; a checkbox field toggles with Space instead.
Move the text cursor by a grapheme, or to the start or end of the text.
Extend the selection by a grapheme.

keyboard.key: Cmd+A, C, X, V (macOS); Ctrl+A, C, X, V (Windows, Linux)
keyboard.outcome: Select all, copy, cut and paste.
A new line in a multi-line input; nothing in a one-line input, whose form submits from its button.

criteria.name: The field's label, the same words as the visible label.
criteria.role: The input's type: text input (VoiceOver: edit text; Narrator: edit; Orca: entry) or checkbox (check box).
criteria.group: The hint, then the error, read after the label; the form's label names the group the field is in.
criteria.state: Required when the field is required, invalid when it carries an error (VoiceOver: invalid data; Narrator: invalid entry; Orca: invalid entry), checked or not for a checkbox.

setting.statement: WHEN I set the system text size to 200% (Windows' Accessibility, Text size; GNOME's Large Text or text scaling factor) I SEE the label, the input's text, the hint and the error grow with it, with no loss of information.

WHEN I raise the display scale (macOS' Displays, Larger Text; Windows' Scale at 150% or 200%; GNOME's Scale at 200%) I SEE the label, the input's text, the hint and the error drawn sharp and larger, whole and without overlapping.

WHEN I turn on the platform's high contrast (macOS' Increase contrast, a Windows contrast theme, the desktop portal's contrast) I SEE the window switch to the high-contrast palette by itself, the label, the input's text, the hint and the error at 7:1.
WHEN I choose the high-contrast theme for the window I SEE the label, the input's text, the hint and the error and its focus ring drawn in the high-contrast palette, every pair at 7:1.
WHEN I magnify the screen (macOS Zoom, Windows Magnifier, GNOME's Zoom) with focus following I SEE the magnifier follow the keyboard focus to the label, the input's text, the hint and the error.

check.statement: WHEN the window opens or loads a screen I SEE it hold the keyboard focus, so Tab reaches the input without a click.
The input is one stop in the window's tab order, and focusing it puts the keyboard focus there.

WHEN I use Tab and Shift+Tab I SEE focus reach the input in reading order, top to bottom, wrapping at either end, on every platform (macOS' Keyboard navigation setting does not change it: the window keeps its own tab order).
WHEN the input has focus I SEE a 2px ring in the focus color drawn outside it, on the window's ground, a pair the palettes hold to 3:1.
I SEE the label stay visible above the input, an asterisk after it when the field is required.
I SEE the hint as text under the input and the error in words, not only in the danger color.
WHEN I compose text with an IME (a Japanese keyboard; Windows+Period; macOS' Ctrl+Cmd+Space) I SEE the marked text in the input, and the composed text entered.
WHEN I press Space on a focused checkbox field I SEE it toggle between ☐ and ☑.
WHEN I Tab to the input with VoiceOver (macOS), Narrator (Windows) or Orca (Linux) I HEAR its label and I HEAR it identify itself as its input type.
WHEN I Tab to the input I HEAR the hint and any error read after the label, and I HEAR it expressed as required or invalid when it is.
WHEN I type, move the cursor or select in the input I HEAR the characters, words or selection the screen reader echoes.
WHEN I toggle a checkbox field I HEAR its new state, checked or not checked.

announce.api: AXTextField (AXTextArea for a text area), its label as the AXTitle (AccessKit Role::TextInput or MultilineTextInput, with its label), the hint and error as its AXHelp (AccessKit described_by), AXRequired, AXInvalid when it carries an error, AXValue and AXSelectedTextRange; a checkbox field AXCheckBox with AXValue 0 or 1.
announce.says: "Email, required, edit text", then the hint; with an error, "invalid data" and the error; a checkbox field "Subscribe, unchecked, checkbox".

announce.api: ControlType Edit, its label as the Name, the hint and error as the HelpText (and DescribedBy), IsRequiredForForm, IsDataValidForForm false when it carries an error, the Value and Text patterns; a checkbox field ControlType CheckBox with the Toggle pattern.
announce.says: "Email, edit, required", then the hint; with an error, "invalid entry" and the error; a checkbox field "Subscribe, check box, not checked".

announce.api: ATSPI_ROLE_ENTRY, its label as the name (and a label-for relation from the label), the hint and error as its description, STATE_REQUIRED, STATE_INVALID_ENTRY when it carries an error, STATE_EDITABLE, the Text and EditableText interfaces; a checkbox field ATSPI_ROLE_CHECK_BOX with STATE_CHECKED.
announce.says: "Email, entry, required", then the hint; with an error, "invalid entry" and the error; a checkbox field "Subscribe, check box, not checked".

criteria.note: GPUI 0.2.2 exposes no accessibility tree (no AccessKit, NSAccessibility, UI Automation or AT-SPI provider), so every HEAR check is blocked by the toolkit, and so are the system text size, the platform's high contrast and a magnifier following focus, which it does not report. GPUI's main branch has AccessKit (zed-industries/zed#56065), not yet released (gpui/README.md, "Accessibility tree"). No CI job runs the window tests that show the SEE checks; they run by hand (ACCESSIBILITY.md).
